messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a spike in outbound TLS rejects from eu-west starting ~08:12 UTC after yesterday's RBAC cleanups. Keystore agent shows a bunch of `keystore.eviction` events and `KMS AccessDenied` unwrap errors. Anyone touching keystore roles?
sec-bot: Alert: keystore-access-denied on proxy-eu-west (count=78) — rule id: KEystore.AccessDenied. Link: https://obs.internal/alerts/859123
jon: @maria I trimmed a few service role bindings last night as part of the RBAC reduction PR (infra#2921). I did not expect keystore agent to rely on one of those roles.
irene: which binding? I removed `keystore-reader:svc-proxy` temporarily for a test. If that was removed cluster-wide, that would explain the unwrap denies.
maria: that sounds likely. Logs show failures at the proxy side before the TLS handshake completes. sample lines: ```
2026-03-21T08:17:03Z proxy-keystore[pid=12]: unwrap failed: AccessDeniedException: Caller not authorized to use key
2026-03-21T08:17:03Z proxy-keystore[pid=12]: evicting cached key alias=projects/redwood/locations/eu-west/keyRings/proxy/cryptoKeys/proxy-key
```
kevin: thumbs up — if the keystore agent can't unwrap, the mTLS handshake fails because the server cert can't be loaded into memory. Quick mitigation: re-add the `keystore-reader:svc-proxy` binding or temporarily grant `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` to the node pool service account for eu-west.
sam: we should avoid giving broad `cryptoKeyDecrypter` to nodes long-term. Suggest two-step: 1) temp binding at the role level for svc-proxy 2) patch keystore agent to fallback to cached cert if KMS unwrap fails for 30s.
jon: agreed. I'm rolling the binding back now. pinging infra-oncall. (reaction :hammer_and_wrench:)
sec-bot: Deployment triggered: infra-rollout/rollback-8591 by jon — started.
kevin: for audit: we need to confirm whether any successful decrypts happened with an unauthorized principal. Query CloudKMS audit logs for methodName=Decrypt and resourceName=proxy-key between 08:00-08:20 UTC. Example GCP log filter: ```
resource.type="k8s_cluster"
protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"
resource.labels.project_id="redwood-prod"
resource.labels.location="eu-west1"
timestamp>="2026-03-21T08:00:00Z"
timestamp<="2026-03-21T08:20:00Z"
```
irene: ran the query — only `principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/projects/infra/serviceAccounts/infra-keystore` had denies. No successful decrypts from unexpected principals. So far looks like a deny-only incident.
maria: that's good news. That reduces blast radius. Still, client sides saw TLS handshake failures. We need a mitigation that avoids global outages when RBAC prunes run.
sam: long-term fix ideas: - make keystore agent resilient to short-term KMS deny (use cached cert with TTL and refresh backoff) - make RBAC change windowed: a dry-run audit that verifies keystore unwraps for each region before commit - add canary to block RBAC PRs that touch keystore-related roles
jon: +1. Also want to add an automated audit check in PR CI: run a `keystore-access-sim` job that uses a read-only token from each affected SA and attempts a decrypt (dry-run) and fails CI if denies.
kevin: vulnerability question: could an attacker trigger mass keystore evictions? If you can change RBAC at scale, yes, but that's a privileged operation. For threat model: we should treat unexpected evictions as high-sev alert and auto-create an incident. Add a detection rule: "keystore.eviction.count > 10 in 5m" -> create incident.
irene: created an incident runbook stub: INCIDENT-KESTORE-8591. Added steps: 1) check KMS decrypt audit 2) rollback RBAC change 3) check for successful unauthorized decrypts 4) rotate affected keys if suspicious 5) notify customers via status page if > 1% TLS error rate.
maria: action items from here?
jon: I rolled back the binding (done). infra-oncall confirmed nodes can decrypt again — keystore agent shows unwrap successes.
kevin: I'll run the CloudKMS audit queries and attach results to the incident ticket.
sam: I'll open a follow-up ticket to implement keystore agent fallback/caching and the CI keystore-access-sim check.
irene: I'll add the detection rule to telemetry and add a short postmortem template into the incident ticket.
maria: thanks team. Post-incident: schedule a short retro with infra and sec to coordinate RBAC change process. (reaction :coffee:)
sec-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-KESTORE-8591; severity=medium; runbook=INCIDENT-KESTORE-8591. Link: https://incidents.internal/INCIDENT-KESTORE-8591
jon: closing thread here but will update the incident with logs and the PR link for the rollback that fixed it.
